summary.text: Courtney Millett is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Kalkallo at the 2026 Victorian election. A teacher at a public school and a union member, Millett lives in Craigieburn and is involved with Socialists In Schools, a union-based group. The campaign centres on public housing, publicly owned services and public education.

priorities.text: one based on care rather than punishment
Building public housing on a large scale and freezing rents
Affordable, publicly owned childcare, health and aged care
Full funding for public schools
Stronger rights for workers and unions

sources.title: Kalkallo: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Courtney Millett, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Eddie Dadisho is the Liberal candidate for Kalkallo at the 2026 Victorian election. He lives in Wallan and works as a compliance manager in banking, and he holds degrees in law and finance from Western Sydney University. The party says he volunteers with his church and has helped give food and clothes to homeless people.

priorities.text: More police and tougher laws on crime
Lower taxes to ease the cost of living
Support for small business
Fully duplicating Donnybrook Road
A plan to get rid of potholes

sources.title: Kalkallo: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Eddie Dadisho, Liberal for Kalkallo, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Jeanette Dobson is the Family First candidate for Kalkallo at the 2026 Victorian election. Her party page says she is married with three daughters and four grandchildren, belongs to a Bible-based church, and is standing because she wants Christian values represented in Parliament. A Jeanette Dobson was the Family First candidate for Evelyn at the 2022 state election; the sources don't say whether it is the same person.

previous_candidacies.note: Matched by name and party only: no source says the 2026 Kalkallo candidate is the person who stood in Evelyn.

priorities.text: A pro-life position, protecting human life before birth through to old age
Bringing Judeo-Christian values back into Victorian public life
Strong families and faith as the base of a healthy society

summary.text: Payal Tiwari is the Greens candidate for Kalkallo at the 2026 Victorian election. An engineer and technology executive who also advises a family violence refuge, she came to Australia from overseas 33 years ago. She contested the federal seat of Holt for the Greens in 2025, winning 11.2 per cent of first preferences.

priorities.text: A train station for Beveridge
Better public transport and roads in the growth suburbs
A secondary school in Beveridge
More support for residents doing it tough

summary.text: Ros Spence has been a Labor member of the Legislative Assembly since 2014, for Yuroke until 2022 and for Kalkallo since. A minister since 2020, she now holds the corrections, youth justice, victim support and community sport portfolios. She is recontesting Kalkallo in 2026.

summary.text: Troy Steans is One Nation's candidate for Kalkallo at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC says he has worked in public transport and the coach industry for over two decades and has been a Country Fire Authority volunteer for upwards of 25 years. One Nation's candidate page refused automated requests, so it could not be checked.
